Qualitative data (n=29) shows broad activity diversity — driving, care-giving, therapy, just listening — suggesting versatile real-world applicability, with 10-minute settle time as dominant. YouTube views at 30 are the highest in the library despite NULL retention data, indicating early reach traction pending engagement validation. AutoGluon predicts 6.859 for this zone — notably below the observed 7.15 — making this the only zone where observed exceeds AutoGluon prediction, suggesting the model under-attributes H-OS-L1's observed efficacy.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall

Qualitative context (n=21) shows 10-minute settle time as dominant with 'Noticeable improvement' as modal change rating and music opinion splitting between 'Liked it' and 'Neutral.' Cross-run drift at 0.780 is moderate, indicating relatively stable analytical framing. YouTube views at 5.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Helps listeners unwind, though reactions to the music are mixed; a steady 10-minute settle is the typical experience.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier

Qualitative context (n=23) shows 'Trying to sleep' as the dominant activity — an interesting crossover use for an over-stimulation protocol — and rhythm opinion is evenly split between 'Balanced / comfortable' and 'Very settling / calming,' indicating a perceptual listener divide. The protocol appears as the most analytically distinct by cross-protocol semantic clustering (mean similarity 0.677), indicating Sphere frames it differently from other protocols. YouTube views at 8; cross-run drift at 0.679 is notable.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Works well for many, including those using it for sleep rather than overstimulation; the rhythm lands differently for different listeners.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow

Qualitative data (n=23) shows predominantly 'Myself' listening with 'Moderate Improvement' as the modal rating, settling around 10 minutes, with strong music approval (10 liked, 6 loved). YouTube reach is minimal at 7 views. AutoGluon predicts 7.838 for the anxiety zone, approximately 0.6 points above observed, with cross-bucket routing to X-ME-L1 and X-MD-L1 suggesting the model sees anxiety protocols as applicable to mood and motivation states. Cross-run drift at 0.665 is notable.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: Most listeners feel calmer within about 10 minutes, with many reporting noticeable relief from anxiety — the data suggests this is a reliable first-stop protocol.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage

H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: Listeners tend to settle a little faster than with L1, often within 5 minutes, making it a good shorter-session option for anxiety.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley

H-AX-L3.sphere_plain: Many listeners find the rhythm deeply calming, though some need the full session to feel the benefit — patience seems to help.

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor

sphere_commentary.overview:
Outcome scores cluster in the 6.5–7.2 range across all series, with TRANSFORMING trailing HEALING and THRIVING by roughly 0.4 points while exhibiting the widest spread — consistent with its ascending-arc design.
• HEALING generates the most robust data (n=574) with the lowest protocol-level variance.
• THRIVING achieves a comparable mean on fewer respondents and reveals a clear level gradient in Focus & Clarity.
• YouTube engagement data is effectively absent across the library, with H-OS-L1 the only protocol exceeding 30 views.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series-level patterns broadly reflect design intent and reveal distinct population-fit profiles.
• HEALING delivers the most consistent listener responses, particularly across Anxiety and Sleep protocols where variance is tight.
• THRIVING shows the highest single protocol mean in the library (T-FC-L3 at 7.63), with a level gradient where L3 outperforms L1 across FC and CF categories.
• TRANSFORMING carries the widest individual protocol spreads and the lowest series mean, with ASCENT protocols underperforming DESCENT and AutoGluon-predicted mood-energy protocol X-ME-L1 markedly exceeding its observed mean.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols show distributional irregularities that warrant targeted investigation rather than judgment.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45) is the lowest-scoring and most variable protocol in the entire library — flagged by all five analyzers.
• T-FC-L3 (n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97) shows a bimodal pattern with a score-10 spike alongside a cluster at 6–8 suggesting a possible subgroup effect.
• T-MB-L2 (n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03) shows the widest variance in THRIVING, with rhythm opinion split between balanced and slightly busy — flagged by multiple analyzers as a potential listener divergence.
• AutoGluon's predicted scores exceed observed means by 1.4–1.5 points for H-CR-L2, X-ME-L1, and X-MD-L1, suggesting a systematic model–observation gap worth investigating.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 — at n=10 and mean 5.70 with std 2.45, this protocol warrants either revision or a decision not to release further iterations pending larger-sample validation.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-MB-L2 — the highest variance in THRIVING (std 2.03) and bimodal rhythm opinion suggest testing an L2 variant with a clearer groove profile.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L3 — AutoGluon cross-bucket routing repeatedly references this protocol from neighboring zones; consider expanding routing or visibility beyond the focus entry.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-CR-L2 — AutoGluon predicts 7.955 against an observed 6.52; investigate early-listener retention before the entrainment curve engages.
• X-ME-L1 — AutoGluon's top predictions for low-affect states (8.23) far exceed observed (6.74); test as a primary TRANSFORMING entry point with revised onboarding context.
• H-CR-L1/L2/L3 — mean scores 6.35–6.52 are structurally expected for crisis entries but qualitative data shows 8 of 24 L1 respondents reporting significant improvement, suggesting the protocol delivers acute relief that the numeric scale undersells.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is pervasive across the library rather than concentrated in a few protocols, suggesting either evolving data patterns or genuine analytical instability across runs.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 20 of 30 protocols show drift below the 0.85 stability threshold, with X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), and T-FC-L3 (0.532) showing the most extreme shifts — warrants monitoring for analytical consistency.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: T-FC-L1↔T-FC-L2 (0.878) and H-SL-L1↔H-SL-L2 (0.869) form the tightest analytical pairs, while H-OS-L3 is the most analytically distinct protocol (mean similarity 0.677).
• Confidence note: embedding data has accumulated across multiple runs but the near-universal drift signals a need for repeated-run validation before treating analytical framings as stable reference points.

Forms the tightest analytical pair with H-SL-L1 (similarity 0.869). Cross-run drift at 0.681 is notable; YouTube views at 5.
by_protocol.H-SL-L3: n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, meaningful confidence. by_protocol.T-CF-L1: n=34, mean=6.74, std=1.73, meaningful confidence. Cross-run drift at 0.730 is notable. YouTube views minimal at 2.
by_protocol.T-CF-L2: n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, meaningful confidence — the tightest Creative Flow distribution. by_protocol.T-CF-L3: n=18, mean=7.28, std=1.32, developing confidence. This is the highest mean in the Creative Flow cluster with the lowest variance, and qualitative context (n=25, larger than outcome n) shows 'Noticeable improvement' as modal change with 5/10-minute settle time split. The protocol appears among the most analytically distinct by semantic clustering (mean similarity 0.693), and cross-run drift at 0.602 is notable — evolving analytical interpretation accompanies the thin data. Treat as a promising signal requiring n growth before pattern conclusions.
by_protocol.T-FC-L1: n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, meaningful confidence — the lowest-scoring Focus & Clarity protocol. Distribution shows early density at scores 3–5 alongside a secondary mode at score 8, suggesting possible population mismatch where some listeners find strong benefit while others do not. Qualitative context shows 'Noticeable improvement' as modal change rating and 'Slightly busy' as the dominant rhythm opinion (9 of 23), which may explain the spread. Pairs tightly with T-FC-L2 in semantic clustering (0.878). Cross-run drift at 0.614 is notable; YouTube views at 5.
by_protocol.T-FC-L2: n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, meaningful confidence — a substantial step up from L1 with a cleaner distribution peaking at score 8 and only one respondent below 4. Qualitative context shows 10-minute settle time as dominant with therapy and care-giving as primary activities. Pairs tightly with T-FC-L1 analytically (similarity 0.878), and cross-run drift at 0.633 is notable. YouTube views at 4.
by_protocol.T-FC-L3: n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, meaningful confidence — the highest-scoring protocol in the entire library by mean. Distribution shows a striking score-10 spike alongside a secondary cluster at 6–8, a bimodal pattern that demands subgroup investigation. by_protocol.T-MB-L1: n=25, mean=7.04, std=1.34, meaningful confidence — the tightest distribution in the Maintenance cluster with a clean mode at score 8 and no scores below 5, indicating consistent if moderate performance. Qualitative context (n=23) reveals 20-minute settle time as dominant — the slowest in the library — which aligns with HOLD protocol architecture and may explain the moderate mean. Therapy session is the dominant activity. Cross-run drift at 0.578 is notable; YouTube views at 3.
by_protocol.T-MB-L2: n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03, meaningful confidence — the widest variance in the THRIVING series. Distribution spreads from score 3 to 10 with no clear concentration; qualitative context shows 'Slightly busy' tied with 'Balanced / comfortable' in rhythm opinion (7 each), a perceptual split that may drive the variance. With only 22 respondents, the 2.03 std signals genuine population heterogeneity warranting larger-n investigation. Cross-run drift at 0.569 is notable; YouTube views at 4.
by_protocol.T-MB-L3: n=14, mean=6.93, std=1.73, developing confidence. Distribution shows an unusual pattern with spikes at scores 8 and 10 but almost nothing in between, and qualitative context (n=19, larger than outcome n) reveals 'Did NOT settle' as a meaningful signal for 4 of 19 respondents — the only protocol where non-settle appears at this frequency and a concerning signal for a maintenance protocol. Cross-run drift at 0.554 is notable. AutoGluon selects this as the maintenance zone lead at 7.693, substantially above observed mean of 6.93.
by_protocol.X-MC-L1: n=24, mean=6.75, std=1.62, meaningful confidence. Cross-run drift at 0.655 is notable; YouTube views at 8.
by_protocol.X-MC-L2: n=16, mean=6.81, std=1.64, developing confidence. Cross-run drift at 0.764 is the highest stability within TRANSFORMING. AutoGluon names this the zone lead at predicted 7.538. YouTube views at 12 are the second-highest in TRANSFORMING.
by_protocol.X-MC-L3: n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, developing confidence — the lowest-scoring protocol in the entire dataset with extreme variance. Given n=10 and developing confidence, treat this mean as highly provisional. YouTube views at 8; cross-run drift at 0.696 is notable.
by_protocol.X-MD-L1: n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, meaningful confidence. Ascent protocol characteristic — wide variance with scores spread 3–10 and 45% positive rate, the lowest in the library. by_protocol.X-MD-L2: n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, developing confidence — distribution concentrated at scores 6–8 with no respondent scoring above 9, an absence of high-end response worth monitoring. by_protocol.X-MD-L3: n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, developing confidence — the highest mean in the Motivation cluster on the smallest n with extreme variance. by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Most listeners feel calmer within about 10 minutes, with many reporting noticeable relief from anxiety — the data suggests this is a reliable first-stop protocol.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Listeners tend to settle a little faster than with L1, often within 5 minutes, making it a good shorter-session option for anxiety.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Many listeners find the rhythm deeply calming, though some need the full session to feel the benefit — patience seems to help.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Designed for acute distress — listeners may arrive in extreme states, but those who respond report significant relief, often within minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: The groove works therapeutically even when the music isn't everyone's taste; take time to settle into the session.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: The fastest onset in the crisis cluster — some listeners feel immediate relief, though the musical style divides opinion.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: A versatile, widely-used protocol — listeners report feeling calmer during driving, caregiving, or just unwinding, often within 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Helps listeners unwind, though reactions to the music are mixed; a steady 10-minute settle is the typical experience.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Works well for many, including those using it for sleep rather than overstimulation; the rhythm lands differently for different listeners.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: A solid sleep-entry protocol — many listeners feel calmer quickly and caregivers often use it during support sessions.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: The rhythm may feel a little busy for some sleep listeners, but caregivers and clinicians report good results.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Calms many within minutes, especially those supporting others; the rhythm feels steady and supportive.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: A gentle nudge toward creative flow — listeners report subtle shifts, often after settling for 10 minutes or so.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Some listeners experience a genuinely significant creative shift, even if the numeric outcome is modest.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: The strongest creative-flow signal in the library, though the data is still developing — early listeners report a real shift.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Helps some focus, though others find the rhythm a touch busy — the experience seems to vary with the listener's state.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: A reliable clarity protocol with a higher mean than L1; many listeners settle well within 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Stands out as the sharpest focus experience — many listeners report significant gains in concentration and calm.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Provides steady balance, though it asks for patience — a 20-minute settle isn't unusual for maintenance protocols.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Responses split — some find it grounding, others feel the rhythm is slightly off; worth trying more than once.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Helpful for some, but a few listeners don't settle at all — the experience seems inconsistent at this stage.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Supports clearer thinking for many, though a small number report it worsened their state — worth noticing how it lands for you.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Settles into a deeply calming groove that many listeners love — a reassuring mind-clarity option.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Mixed and provisional — the data here is too thin to draw firm conclusions, though some listeners benefit.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Tries to lift motivation but results vary widely — those who respond tend to feel it within 5 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Takes longer to settle and outcomes are inconsistent — a developing protocol that may need more time and tuning.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Some listeners feel quickly uplifted while others don't connect — the variability is real and the data is still early.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Supports mood and energy for many listeners, though the model predicts it should do better — there's likely untapped potential here.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Many listeners feel a quick and significant lift in mood — a quietly strong protocol for low-affect states.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Lifts some listeners while leaving others untouched — mixed settling times and an inconsistent experience at this stage.
